questions.question: What did Michelangelo carve as a gift to the prior of Santo Spirito in 1493?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in the months following Lorenzo de' Medici's death, Michelangelo carved a polychrome wooden Crucifix as a gift to the prior of Santo Spirito.
Incorrect. The Hercules statue was carved between 1493 and 1494 after he bought a block of marble, not as a gift to the prior.
Incorrect. The Madonna of the Stairs was sculpted from 1490 to 1492 at the Platonic Academy, not as a gift to the prior.
Incorrect. The sleeping Cupid was made during his half-year in Florence around 1495, not as a gift to the prior of Santo Spirito.

questions.question: Who invited Michelangelo to Rome after discovering that the sleeping Cupid was a modern work rather than an ancient one?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Cardinal Raffaele Riario discovered the fraud but was so impressed by the quality that he invited Michelangelo to Rome.
Incorrect. Lorenzo di Pierfrancesco de' Medici asked Michelangelo to make the Cupid look buried so it could be passed off as ancient, but he did not invite Michelangelo to Rome.

questions.question: Which architectural project did Michelangelo begin leading at age 71?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that at the age of 71, Michelangelo succeeded Antonio da Sangallo the Younger as the architect of St. Peter's Basilica.
Incorrect. The Laurentian Library's design pioneered Mannerist architecture, but there is no mention of Michelangelo beginning it at age 71.
Incorrect. The Sistine Chapel ceiling is a fresco, not an architectural project he began leading at age 71.
Incorrect. The Shrine of St. Dominic involved small figures Michelangelo carved in Bologna, not an architectural project at age 71.

questions.question: What did Michelangelo gain while living with a stonecutter in Settignano?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that while living with a nanny and her husband, a stonecutter, in Settignano, the young boy gained his love for working marble.
Incorrect. Training in fresco painting came later during his apprenticeship with Domenico Ghirlandaio.
Incorrect. Knowledge of Humanist philosophy came from the Platonic Academy under the Medicis.
Incorrect. The apprenticeship with Ghirlandaio began in 1488 in Florence, not in Settignano.

questions.question: What happened to Michelangelo's nose when he was 17?
options: It was struck by Pietro Torrigiano, causing disfigurement.
It was broken in a fall from scaffolding.
It was injured while carving the David.
It was disfigured by chisel dust.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that when he was 17, another pupil, Pietro Torrigiano, struck him on the nose, causing the disfigurement conspicuous in portraits.
Incorrect. The article does not mention a fall from scaffolding.
Incorrect. The article does not mention an injury while carving the David.
Incorrect. The article does not mention chisel dust disfiguring his nose.

questions.question: Why did Michelangelo leave Florence in 1494?
options: The Medici were expelled following the rise of Savonarola.
He was summoned by Cardinal Riario to work in Rome.
He wanted to study anatomy in Bologna.
He completed the David and moved to Rome.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in 1494 the Medici were expelled from Florence as a result of the rise of Savonarola, and Michelangelo left the city before the end of the political upheaval.
Incorrect. Cardinal Riario invited him to Rome after the Cupid incident, which occurred after he had already left Florence.
Incorrect. He studied anatomy in Bologna after leaving Florence, but that was not the reason he left.
Incorrect. The David was completed in 1504, long after he left Florence in 1494.
